Rietweg 25: restaining and repairing the exterior wood

Scope and cost estimate for cleaning, restaining and repairing every exterior timber surface, built from the 3D model's geometry, the owner photos and the inspection findings. Prices researched on 27 November 2026. Every rate below can be changed and the totals update.

Plan of the house from the 3D model, north up. Shaded areas are roofs; squares are the veranda posts. Tap a wall to jump to it.

  • Restain, don't replace. The dark-brown stain is worn thin and faded wherever weather reaches it. The photos show no peeling, warped or split boards and no visible rot. That is a normal end of cycle for rough-sawn spruce.
  • Worst walls: the guest wing's north gable on the entrance walk and the main house's south gable by the pool. The walls under the veranda and loggia roofs only need one coat.
  • Real repair risk is at the bottom. Where boards run onto paving (forecourt, garage doors, link entrance, veranda) their ends soak up splash water. How many are soft is the largest unknown in this estimate.
  • One veranda post stands directly on the paving. It gets a stand-off foot.
  • Plan it for May to September 2027. Book painters in January or February.

Trims, posts, doors and decks

Garage doors and plank door

Two garage doors faced with the same boards (10.5 m² in the model) and one plank side door. Both garage doors stop on the cobbles.

Fix: wash, two coats; seal and if needed shorten the bottom rail.

Veranda and loggia posts and beams

Six posts about 14 × 14 cm, five on stone pads and one directly on the paving (207644AC). About 23 m of beam over them.

Fix: two coats; prop the low post, cut it 3 to 4 cm clear and set it on a post base.

Roof edges and soffits

About 60 m of verge boards on the four gables and 98 m of eaves with exposed rafter ends. 141 m² of soffits and covered ceilings measured on the slope; exposed rafters add about a third more surface.

Fix: verges and eave ends two coats, soffits and ceilings one coat from the gable scaffold and a tower.

Pool deck

Grey weathered hardwood with screwed boards. 21 m² in the model; the photos look wider, so 24 m² is priced. No lifted or split boards visible.

Fix: clean, swap 2 to 4 boards, re-screw; oil only if you want the brown back (grey is fine for hardwood).

Raised beds, swing, bollards

Untreated and silver-grey by design. Not priced: they are garden items, not part of the house.

Check: push and probe the log swing posts at ground level; if soft, replace the frame before children use it.

How the work is done

  1. ProtectCover windows, paving, gravel and plants; mask the chimney and lamps.
  2. ProbeScrewdriver test along every bottom edge; mark soft boards.
  3. WashWood cleaner or algae wash, brushed in, rinsed at low pressure. Never a jet.
  4. DryTwo to three dry days; wood under about 18% moisture.
  5. RepairReplace soft boards, cut bottom edges clear, swap rusty nails.
  6. PrepareBrush off loose fibres; prime new boards and cut ends.
  7. StainCoat 1, overnight, coat 2. Brush into every gap and edge.
Product. Ask the seller what was used last time and keep to that system. If nobody knows, a test patch on the guest wing north gable shows whether a solvent-based glaze (Remmers HK-Lasur, Sikkens Cetol Filter 7) or an oil glaze (Osmo Öl-Lasur) takes. The tone is a dark walnut to ebony.

Tax: if you are taxed in Germany, 20% of the labour on your own home's maintenance, up to €6,000 of labour a year, comes off your income tax (§35a EStG, worth up to €1,200). The invoice must show labour separately and be paid by bank transfer. A cut to 15% has been proposed but is not law. [ZDH]

Restain or replace?

Full re-cladding means stripping 445 m² of boards and doors, disposing of about 5 tonnes of old timber, checking the membrane and battens, fixing new pre-stained boards, and scaffolding every wall instead of only the gables. The trims, soffits, posts and decks still need the same treatment. It is only worth it if the probe test finds soft boards across whole walls, or the battens behind are wet. A single bad wall can be re-clad on its own, at roughly extra for the guest wing north gable, but new boards will look different from the weathered ones for several years.

Before contract: checks on site

About an hour with a screwdriver, binoculars and a wet cloth. These narrow the biggest unknowns.

  • Press a screwdriver into the lowest 30 cm of boards at the link entrance, the forecourt and garage doors, the veranda and the south gable. Count the boards that give.
  • Probe the foot of each veranda post, especially the one standing on the paving.
  • Rub a wet cloth on both north gables. Brown on the cloth means stain is left; green means algae.
  • Look at the verge boards and rafter ends with binoculars for cracks and bare grey wood.
  • Check nail heads for rust streaks, and press boards near the nail lines for movement.
  • Ask the seller when the cladding was last stained, by whom, with which product and colour, and for any leftover tins.
  • Walk the pool deck by the coping and look for loose screws and soft board ends.
  • Push hard on the swing frame and probe its posts at ground level.
  • Look at the guest wing south gable and the main house west wall, which no photo shows closely.
What this estimate can't see. Rot inside boards, the membrane and battens behind them, whether the air gap has insect mesh, what product is on the wood, and close-ups of the north walls. Eave and verge trims are assumed timber; any that are metal come out of the price.
